subject: Business Models
title: Webvan: Too Early, Too Big
description: One-minute skill: Webvan: Too Early, Too Big.

hook.text: Webvan raised $800 million to deliver groceries online in 1999. It burned through all of it in 18 months.

buildup.text: Webvan built massive automated warehouses in 10 cities before proving demand in even one city.

discovery.text: The model required enormous capital: warehouses, delivery trucks, cold chains—all before a single profitable order.

twist.text: Twenty years later, Instacart proved the model works—using existing stores and gig drivers. No warehouses needed.

climax.text: Webvan's idea was right but its model was wrong. Capital-light delivery beat capital-heavy warehouse-first.

punchline.text: $800M, 18 months, bankrupt. Right idea, wrong decade, wrong model.

quiz.question: What was Webvan's key strategic mistake?
options: Building massive infrastructure before proving demand
